slides.title: Float or Sink? 🌊
slides.text: When we place an object in water, it either FLOATS on top or SINKS to the bottom! A leaf floats like a boat, but a stone sinks like an anchor!
slides.spoken: When we place an object in water, it either floats on top or sinks to the bottom! A leaf floats like a boat, but a stone sinks like an anchor!

slides.title: Why Do Things Float? 🍃
slides.text: Objects like wooden blocks, corks, and plastic balls float because they are light for their size or trap air inside them!
slides.spoken: Objects like wooden blocks, corks, and plastic balls float because they are light for their size or trap air inside them!

slides.title: Why Do Things Sink? 🪨
slides.text: Objects like stones, metal coins, and iron keys sink because they are heavy and solid, packed with material with no air inside!
slides.spoken: Objects like stones, metal coins, and iron keys sink because they are heavy and solid, packed with material with no air inside!

slides.title: The Great Iron Ship! 🚢
slides.text: A tiny iron nail sinks at once! Yet a huge iron ship floats across the ocean! Why? Because the ship is hollow and full of air inside, making it light for its size!
slides.spoken: A tiny iron nail sinks at once! Yet a huge iron ship floats across the ocean! Why? Because the ship is hollow and full of air inside, making it light for its size!

slides.title: Predict, Test, Record! 📋
slides.text: A little scientist always predicts what will happen before testing! We test in a bowl of water, record our observations in a table, and sort our objects into floaters and sinkers!
slides.spoken: A little scientist always predicts what will happen before testing! We test in a bowl of water, record our observations in a table, and sort our objects into floaters and sinkers!

challenges.question: What does it mean when an object FLOATS in water?
challenges.answer: It stays on top of the water
options: It stays on top of the water
It goes to the bottom
It disappears completely
challenges.hint: Think of a leaf or a wooden boat resting on a pond surface!
challenges.misconception: Floating means the object stays on top of the water! It does not drop down to the bottom. The leaf or wooden block rests on the surface like a small raft!

challenges.question: What does it mean when an object SINKS in water?
challenges.answer: It goes to the bottom of the water
options: It stays on top of the water
It goes to the bottom of the water
It floats away in the air
challenges.hint: Think of a heavy stone or metal coin dropped into a bowl!
challenges.misconception: Sinking means the object drops down through the water and rests at the bottom, like a stone or metal coin falling straight down like an anchor!

challenges.question: Drag each everyday object to the correct bin! Does it float or sink?
challenges.hint: Wood, leaves, cork, and plastic balls stay on top (Float)! Stones, coins, and keys go to the bottom (Sink)!
challenges.misconception: Remember: being heavy or light alone does not decide everything, but wood and plastic balls float while stones and metal coins sink!

challenges.question: Why does a wooden block float while a heavy stone sinks?
challenges.answer: Wood is light for its size and stone is heavy and solid
options: Wood is light for its size and stone is heavy and solid
Wood is always smaller than stones
Stones are painted black
challenges.hint: Think about whether the object is light for its size or packed with heavy solid material!
challenges.misconception: Being heavy or light alone does not fully decide it, but a wooden block is light for its size while a stone is packed full of heavy solid material with no air spaces!

challenges.question: Drag each clue! Does it describe why objects float or why they sink?
challenges.hint: Light, hollow, and air-filled objects float! Heavy, solid, and compact objects sink!
challenges.misconception: Clues for floating: light for its size, has air inside, hollow! Clues for sinking: solid, heavy for its size, packed with material with no air!

challenges.question: A tiny iron nail sinks at once, but a huge iron SHIP floats! Why?
challenges.answer: The ship is hollow and full of air inside
options: The ship is hollow and full of air inside
The ship is made of soft wood disguised as iron
The ship is too fast for water to catch
challenges.hint: Think about what is inside the ship hull — empty space filled with air!
challenges.misconception: A heavy ship floats because it is hollow and full of air inside, making the whole ship light for its size — just like an upside-down bowl trapping air!

challenges.question: Sort these special objects: Feather, Sponge (dry), Metal Key, Gold Ring!
challenges.hint: Feather is extremely light and floats! Dry sponge is full of air and floats! Metal key and gold ring are heavy solid metals and sink!
challenges.misconception: A dry sponge floats because it is full of air holes! Metal keys and gold rings sink because they are dense solid metals with no air!
